title: Coefficient transport of section invariants and normalized deformation comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $n\geq1$, put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, and let $R\to B$ be a unital map to a finite commutative ring. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their bounded intrinsically constructible finite-Tor subcategories [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and the constructible adjoints $Rg_{!,D}\dashv g_D^!$ for $D=R,B$ [sk-prop-sf-existence, sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. For $D=R,B$, write $D_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ for the constant ring sheaf on the small etale site, and define $D_T(1)=\nu_T^*(\mu_{\ell^n,T}\otimes_{R_{T,\mathrm{et}}}D_{T,\mathrm{et}})$, where $\nu_T$ is the small pro-etale to etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $\mu_{\ell^n,T}$ is the etale sheaf $U\mapsto\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^{\ell^n}=1\}$, with $R$ acting by powers, as in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; put $D_T(0)=D_T$ and $D_T(r)=D_T(1)^{\otimes_D r}$ for $r>0$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These are the locally free rank-one Tate lines and canonical pullback identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Fix the coefficient-independent compactifications of these morphisms in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $(-)_B$ for [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] and $c_g:(g_R^!R_S)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}g_B^!B_S$ for the counit-characterized comparison of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional].

For a smooth separated map [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] $g:V\to S$ of pure relative dimension $r\geq0$ with a closed section $s:S\to V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], $g\circ s=1_S$, put $C_D(g,s)=Ls^*g_D^!D_S$. Let $D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ be the geometric deformation space $\operatorname{Bl}_{s(S)\times\{0\}}(V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S)\setminus\widetilde{V\times\{0\}}$ (the tilde denotes strict transform), with its induced smooth map $\widetilde g$ and section $\widetilde s$. Here [def-pur-dnc-section-family] specifies the coefficient-independent geometric deformation space, its structural map and its section; let $\pi_N:N_s\to S$ be the actual normal-bundle projection with zero section $0_N:S\to N_s$ [def-pur-normal-bundle]. Put $F_D=L\widetilde s^*\widetilde g_D^!D_{\mathbf A^1_S}$ for each $D=R,B$. At $D=R$ this is the family object of [def-pur-dnc-section-family] at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and level $n$; the displayed formula defines the corresponding object at the arbitrary finite ring $B$. Use affine space [def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ and $i_j:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ ($j=0,1$) be the projection and its two sections. Identify the fibres with $C_D(g,s)$ and $C_D(\pi_N,0_N)$ using the canonical smooth base-change exchanges (mates of compact-support base change). Define
$$q_{g,s}:(C_R(g,s))_B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B(g,s),\qquad q_F:(F_R)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}F_B$$
by the canonical pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] followed by $Ls^*c_g$, respectively $L\widetilde s^*c_{\widetilde g}$.

For any smooth separated $k$-morphism $g_0:V_0\to S_0$ of pure relative dimension $r_0\geq0$ between schemes in the same setting, with no section assumed, let $h:S'_0\to S_0$ be any $k$-morphism from a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Put $V'_0=V_0\times_{S_0}S'_0$, and write $g'_0:V'_0\to S'_0$ and $h_V:V'_0\to V_0$ for the projections. Write $c_{g_0}$ and $c_{g'_0}$ for the same counit-characterized comparisons defined above. The canonical smooth base-change exchanges $e_D:h_V^*g_{0,D}^!D_{S_0}\to(g'_0)_D^!D_{S'_0}$ are isomorphisms. The coefficient comparisons commute with this exchange, namely, under the canonical pullback/tensor identifications,
$$e_B\circ h_V^*c_{g_0}=c_{g'_0}\circ(e_R)_B.$$ In particular $q_{g,s}$ and $q_F$ respect the two displayed fibre identifications and the corresponding comparisons for the normal-bundle pair. They also respect etale localization of pairs. On a standard coordinate pair $(\mathbf A^r_S\to S,0)$ they are the canonical identification $(R_S(r)[2r])_B\simeq B_S(r)[2r]$.

Let $\kappa_R:F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_R(g,s)$ be the normalized family comparison of [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy], applied at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and level $n$. Under pullback/tensor identifications, the map
$$\kappa_B=a^*q_{g,s}\circ(\kappa_R)_B\circ q_F^{-1}:F_B\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_B(g,s)$$
is the unique isomorphism whose restriction at $i_1$ is the identity under the canonical fibre identification. On each etale coordinate chart carrying the pair near its section to the standard pair, this isomorphism is the constant-family identification normalized to the identity at $t=1$; these restrictions specify the direct coordinate comparison over $B$. Consequently, writing $\delta_D:C_D(g,s)\to C_D(\pi_N,0_N)$ for the inverse of $i_0^*\kappa_D$, one has
$$\delta_B\circ q_{g,s}=q_{\pi_N,0_N}\circ(\delta_R)_B.$$
These assertions include relative dimension zero and the zero coefficient ring.

source.place: Proof (2), coefficient independence of the deformation comparison; made precise using sk-thm-dnc/thm-pur-dnc-invariance.proof.md and prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy.proof.md

proof.text: Choose $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, with uniformizer $\ell$, so the level-$n$ coefficient ring in the purity conventions is $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The unital map $R\to B$ implies $\ell^nB=0$. The unit $R_T$ is a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex, free of rank one in degree zero. Apply [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] to $g$, to $\widetilde g$, and to the normal-bundle projection, using the same fixed compactification at both rings. The smoothness and relative dimension of $\widetilde g$, and its normal-bundle fibre, are given by [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1),(2); these are statements about the geometric space, applied at $R$, so no assertion of that lemma at arbitrary coefficients is being assumed. All the maps to which the coefficient comparison is applied have separated finite-type source and target by our scheme setting. Pulling $c_g$ back along $s$, and $c_{\widetilde g}$ along $\widetilde s$, with the natural tensor/pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], gives exactly $q_{g,s}$ and $q_F$ of the statement. They are isomorphisms because every factor is an isomorphism. The same defines $q_{\pi_N,0_N}$.

source.place: Proof (2), coefficient comparisons for the section and family objects

proof.text:
Apply [det-sp-mixed-base-change] with $f=g_0$, $u=h_V$, $v=h$, $f'=g'_0$, $A=R$, and $K=R_{S_0}$. The unit is eligible for its $D^b_{ctf}$ hypothesis. Its exceptional comparison is explicitly the transpose of the pulled-back counit composed with inverse compact-support base change, exactly the exchange specified in this item; its statement gives that exchange as an isomorphism. Its second identity reads
$$c_{g'_0}(h^*R_{S_0})\,(e_R)_B=e_B\,h_V^*c_{g_0}.$$
Identify $h^*R_{S_0}=R_{S'_0}$, $(R_{S_0})_B=B_{S_0}$, and $h^*B_{S_0}=B_{S'_0}$, to get the required equation. This application does not put a section on $g_0$. In particular, apply it to $\widetilde g$ along each $i_j$, and then pull back along the fibre section. Denote the canonical fibre identifications by $\eta_{j,D}:i_j^*F_D\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{j,D}$, with $C_{1,D}=C_D(g,s)$ and $C_{0,D}=C_D(\pi_N,0_N)$. The geometric fibre descriptions are [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1). The tensor comparison and the composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identify the sources, and give the explicit commutative fibre equations
$$\eta_{j,B}\,i_j^*q_F=q_j\,(\eta_{j,R})_B,\qquad q_1=q_{g,s},\quad q_0=q_{\pi_N,0_N}.$$
Thus the comparisons respect the specified fibres, rather than merely some abstract isomorphisms between the fibre objects. The same application for an etale base localization of the pair gives its base-localization compatibility.

source.place: Proof (2), diagonal/base-change step; mixed base change applied to the two family fibres

proof.text:
Check also the source-coordinate localizations, with their specified adjunction identifications. On an etale coordinate chart of a smooth map $g=p_r e$, [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] identifies $c_g$ with
$$(e^*p_r^*R(r)[2r])_B\xrightarrow{\sim}e^*p_r^*B(r)[2r].$$
Its chart identification preserves the counit (the etale fibre sum followed by the specified affine-space counit). Hence this is the coefficient comparison for those actual chart adjunctions. Pulling to the section gives the canonical coefficient identification of the section Tate line; applying the same chart clause to $\widetilde g$ gives the corresponding identification for the family. The local coordinates of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2),(4) are $x_k=tu_k$; the section is $u_k=0$, so the family chart has the same ordered affine projection with base $\mathbf A^1$. The free-line and shift clauses of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], together with the pullback identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], show that these identifications commute with further restriction and with one another: on a local free generator the map is $x\otimes b\mapsto b x$, and both orders of pullback and scalar extension give that map. Thus $q_{g,s},q_F$ respect etale coordinate localization of pairs. For $e=1$ this proves their asserted standard-pair value $(R_S(r)[2r])_B\simeq B_S(r)[2r]$. No smooth-purity theorem over arbitrary $B$ is used to obtain this normalization.

source.place: Proof (2), the counit-preserving chart description and the vector-bundle/deformation models

proof.text:
By [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy] at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and level $n$, the given $\kappa_R$ is an isomorphism with $i_1^*\kappa_R=1_{C_R(g,s)}$ under $\eta_{1,R}$. Scalar extension is a functor by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], so it preserves this identity and inverses. Define
$$\kappa_B=a^*q_{g,s}\,(\kappa_R)_B\,q_F^{-1}.$$
This is an isomorphism by Step 1. Pull back its formula to $i_1$. Use $i_1^*a^*=1$ and the equation for $j=1$ in Step 2: after the fibre identifications the resulting map is
$$q_{g,s}\,1_{(C_R(g,s))_B}\,q_{g,s}^{-1}=1_{C_B(g,s)}.$$
This proves normalization at $t=1$ for precisely the canonical fibre identification. The algebra here uses only functoriality and cancellation of isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof (2), scalar extension and normalization of the family comparison

proof.text: We prove uniqueness over $B$ without applying a fixed-coefficient uniqueness theorem with an ineligible coefficient ring. By [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy](1) the objects $F_R$ and $C_R(g,s)$ are finite locally constant rank-one $R$-sheaves, with a common shift $[2r]$ (absorb the rank-one Tate twist into the sheaf). By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](1),(3), their scalar extensions are actual finite locally constant rank-one $B$-sheaves with the same shift; Step 1 identifies them with $F_B$ and $C_B(g,s)$. In particular $F_B[-2r]$ and $a^*C_B(g,s)[-2r]$ are ordinary finite locally constant $B$-module sheaves. Pullback preserves the local constant models, and the Tate identification is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Let $\lambda:F_B\to a^*C_B(g,s)$ be any other isomorphism normalized at $t=1$. Remove the common shift. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] both $\lambda$ and $\kappa_B$ are uniquely ordinary $B$-module sheaf maps. Restrict their difference to $R$-module sheaves. On a trivializing cover the underlying module is the finite $R$-module $B$; hence these are finite locally constant $R$-module sheaves, with no requirement that $B$ be free or perfect over $R$. The section $i_1$ meets every connected component of $\mathbf A^1_S$ by [lem-pur-a1-components](2) when $S$ is nonempty. At a geometric point in each such intersection the difference vanishes, since $i_1^*\lambda=i_1^*\kappa_B$. Apply [lem-pur-lisse-morphism-rigidity](2), with coefficient $R=A_{\mathbf Q_\ell,n}$, to conclude the difference is zero. Equality of the underlying $R$-module maps is equality of the $B$-module maps, and full faithfulness restores equality in the derived category. If $S$ is empty all the sheaves and morphisms in this argument are unique, so the same conclusion holds. This proves the claimed uniqueness.

source.place: Proof (2), comparisons determined by normalization at t=1; expanded rigidity argument

proof.text: On the standard pair the family geometry in [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4) is the constant family $\mathbf A^r_S\times_S\mathbf A^1_S$, with section $u=0$. Its pullback comparison $F_R\simeq a^*C_R$ restricts to the identity at $t=1$, so it is $\kappa_R$ by the uniqueness clause of [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy]. On an etale coordinate chart of a general pair, the counit-preserving affine identifications in Step 3 likewise identify both $F_D$ and $a^*C_D$ with the same pulled-back Tate line $D(r)[2r]$, for $D=R,B$. The constant-family comparison is the identity between these two models, normalized at $t=1$. Since the coefficient comparisons on these models are the canonical free-line maps of Step 3, conjugating the $R$ identity by $q_F$ and $a^*q_{g,s}$ gives the $B$ identity. Equivalently, it is the unique normalized map by Step 5 applied over the chart base (which can be chosen affine, separated and finite type over $k$). The local $B$ maps therefore are exactly the restrictions of the global $\kappa_B$ constructed in Step 4. On overlaps they agree as restrictions of that map; after removing $[2r]$ they are sheaf maps by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], and [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] says their global sheaf map is uniquely specified by these restrictions. This is the direct coordinate comparison over $B$. Thus no descent of arbitrary derived morphisms, and no assertion that arbitrary isomorphisms of lines coincide, is hidden in the chart-to-global assertion.

source.place: Proof (2), agreement on coordinate charts and uniqueness of the global normalized comparison

proof.text:
Put $T_D:C_D(\pi_N,0_N)\to C_D(g,s)$ equal to $i_0^*\kappa_D$ after the prescribed fibre identifications, so $\delta_D=T_D^{-1}$. Pull back $\kappa_B q_F=a^*q_{g,s}(\kappa_R)_B$ along $i_0$. The $j=0$ equation in Step 2 and $i_0^*a^*=1$ give
$$T_B q_{\pi_N,0_N}=q_{g,s}(T_R)_B.$$
Multiply on the left by $T_B^{-1}$ and on the right by $(T_R^{-1})_B$. Since scalar extension preserves inverses, this gives exactly
$$\delta_B q_{g,s}=q_{\pi_N,0_N}(\delta_R)_B.$$
This calculation also checks the direction of $\delta_D$ in the statement. All constructions allow $r=0$: the Tate line is $D_S$ and the shift is $[0]$, and the same fibre and cancellation equations apply. For $B=0$, the category of unital $B$-module sheaves has only its zero object and its unique map; $B$ is still the finite underlying $R$-module in Step 5. Thus all isomorphism, normalization and uniqueness assertions include the zero ring.

split_report.summary: Seven-step proof with no new nodes. Reuses the existing mixed-base-change coefficient square, writes both fibre equations, checks the counit-preserving affine coordinate normalization, constructs the conjugated family comparison, proves uniqueness over arbitrary finite B by restricting finite local systems to R and applying rigidity, and calculates the t=0 specialization. No statement change; empty base, relative dimension zero, nonflat coefficients and the zero ring are explicit.
